input.quote: Commerce One hereby grants to Corio a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), right and license in the Territory
input.rationale: The Section 2 grants run to Corio only; the word \"affiliate\" appears nowhere in the Agreement and there is no mechanism to add affiliates, so the fallback element of affiliate coverage on written notice fails on a material term. The other fallback element is already satisfied: the grants are transferable in accordance with Section 14.1, which permits assignment on a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all related assets without consent (the direct-competitor consent carve-out is a minor shortfall noted only). We therefore target the fallback with a single short clause extending the Section 2 licences to our affiliates on written notice; the perpetual/irrevocable and uncured-breach-only termination features of the preferred position are already largely present and are not pursued further.

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
mappings.quote: either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent

ops.text: Affiliates. Upon written notice to Commerce One, the licenses granted to Corio under this Section 2 shall extend to Corio's affiliates.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Section 2 licences run to Corio alone, so we added a short provision extending them to our affiliates on written notice to Commerce One; successor transfer in an M&A transaction is already permitted under Section 14.1.
proposal.summary: Extend the Section 2 licences to Corio affiliates on written notice
